transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Perf), Daniel (Novara ML), Sana (Novara Cloud), Liam (Novara CTO), Marta (Data Ops)

Auto-summary:
Maya: quick recap of last week's changes, we pushed a kv-cache tweak and adjusted continuous batching window. Ethan: ran a 24h lab run with mixed prompt lengths. Customer ran baseline against CloudScale and shared numbers earlier in the day.

[00:00] Maya: all right hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we got the updated numbers in front of us. i think we'll start with a 2 minute recap of what changed since last sync.
[00:14] Daniel: yeah thanks, quick note we also patched our harness to include more short prompts like UI-microinteractions so baseline numbers shift a bit.
[00:23] Ethan: cool — so on the redwood side we changed two knobs: smaller batching window for low-latency lanes and enabled prefix/kv caching for repeated contexts. that gave us a pretty clear p50 win on the 8-128 token bucket.
[00:41] Priya: just to add, we also tried a 4-bit quantized runtime for the high-throughput runner, the quality delta looked acceptable on our eval set but we saw some tail latency variability under peak concurrent loads.
[00:58] Sana: can you remind us what 'tail variability' means practically? we care about SLA for interactive agents — 99th percentile spikes hurt UX.
[01:10] Ethan: yeah so p95/p99 was stable on single-session traffic, but when we push sustained 500 concurrent connections the GPU scheduler occasionally creates small stalls — we traced to kernel launch contention when the kv-cache hot paths get fragmented.
[01:29] Liam: so are those stalls something we can tune or is it inherent to 4-bit quantization?
[01:38] Priya: a little of both — quant helps throughput but can add jitter if memory access pattern changes. we have mitigations: tweak batching thresholds or route high-concurrency traffic to a less-quantized instance type.
[01:52] Daniel: looking at the spreadsheet you sent, p50 delta vs CloudScale is roughly -18ms for medium prompts, p95 about -30ms. but throughput at 500 concurrent shows CloudScale handling a slightly higher RPS. correct?
[02:08] Maya: that's right, the lab run shows that Redwood has better single-request latency for most common prompts but CloudScale's distributed multi-tenant scheduler currently edges us at raw sustained RPS with default configs.
[02:20] Ethan: worth noting we were on a single dedicated slot config in the lab and their benchmark used a larger pooled instance layout — apples to oranges a bit.
[02:30] Mana (sic) [Martha? background voice]: (inaudible)
[02:34] Marta: sorry, typo, i'm Marta — we did a quick overlay of CPU/Network on CloudScale and they had slightly higher NIC credits, which explains their RPS advantage in the baseline.
[02:46] Maya: ok cool so what did you all want to prioritize this week — more latency wins or throughput?
[02:53] Daniel: latency, our product is interactive triage and p50/p95 matter more to users. but CTO caveat: if throughput becomes a blocker on peak, we'll need the dedicated path.
[03:06] Liam: also security note — before any dedicated slots we need SSO + audit logs in the private control plane.
[03:13] Maya: understood, we'll include the Redwood Private checklist in the doc share.
[03:18] Ethan: for today's tuning we tried these three configs: A) low-latency: micro-batch=8, kv-cache aggressive, no quant; B) balanced: micro-batch=16, kv-cache medium, 4-bit quant on background pool; C) high-throughput: micro-batch=32, aggressive quant, cached prefixes only.
[03:36] Daniel: and which one maps to the numbers in the sheet?
[03:39] Ethan: the p50-p95 wins in the sheet are from A, the high throughput line is from C. Balanced is what we recommend for production if you need some throughput with low latency.
[03:50] Sana: we tested A and saw good p50, but under our traffic replay with spiky bursts the p99 jumped, which aligns with your kernel contention note.
[04:03] Priya: quick mitigation: route spike traffic to the background pool (balanced) and burst to dedicated slots with autoscale. that should keep p50 low while smoothing tail.
[04:14] Daniel: can you quantify how many dedicated slots we'd need? CloudScale claims 3 nodes for our 90k daily active users, is that comparable?
[04:23] Ethan: rough calc: for your 10 TPS peak and 200ms target p50 we estimate 2 dedicated GPUs with burst buffer, 3 if you want headroom and lower p99. we will supply a binpack estimator in the sheet.
[04:37] Maya: i'll add that to the next deck.
[04:40] [06:12] (mid-call, screen share mentioned) Maya: linking the bench sheet here: https://redwood.ai/novara/pilot-bench (note: internal link) — raw CSVs in the second tab.
[06:28] Daniel: seeing raw logs now, i think we can run a 10k request sweep overnight comparing the A config vs your recommended balanced; we'll post results.
[06:37] Ethan: perfect — please use the seeded prompt set we attached earlier so quality match is consistent.
[06:45] Marta: small note on network — we saw 7–10ms variance when traffic crossed region boundary; VPC peering would remove that.
[06:56] Maya: are you able to open a VPC peer request this week?
[07:01] Sana: yes we'll kick that off, expect a request by Monday.
[07:09] Liam: procurement question: pricing delta for dedciated vs hosted — can you send a simple TCO model?
[07:15] Maya: yes, we'll send a TCO with committed slots vs pay-as-you go, and include a 6-month break-even.
[07:22] Daniel: any quality regressions from quant? we ran evals but want a human review on a 200-sample set.
[07:30] Priya: for the 4-bit profile the rouge/bleu-ish metrics were within thresholds but we flagged 12/200 for weird truncation on long completions, we can exclude those flows from quantized pool.
[07:43] Ethan: also note function calling payloads with heavy JSON structures showed slightly higher tokenization overhead; we recommend stripping large system prompts into cached prefixes.
[07:58] Daniel: ok makes sense — share example prompt rewrite?
[08:02] Maya: will attach two examples in the post-call notes.
[08:07] [20:10] (later section, tuning discussion) Ethan: we ran a burst test at 500 concurrent for 10 minutes and saw sustained RPS of ~1.2k with config C, but p95 moved from 220ms to 380ms. CloudScale remained at ~1.35k RPS with p95 ~330ms on their baseline.
[20:29] Daniel: that's within tolerance for some workflows but not interactive triage.
[20:35] Priya: exactly — so a hybrid traffic split where interactive goes to low-latency lane and batch/async goes to quantized pool is our recommendation.
[20:46] Liam: does Redwood support dynamic routing by route? we'll need SDK hooks.
[20:51] Maya: yes, the SDK supports route-level policies and can route by header. we'll share sample code.
[20:58] Maya: i'm going to recap next steps now — we captured action items: Maya will send raw logs and TCO, Ethan will send config recommendations and example prompt-rewrites, Daniel/Sana will run the 10k sweep and start VPC peer.
[21:12] Daniel: ok we'll add results by 7/16 and if numbers hold we'll request a dedicated-slot trial for the week of 7/20.
[21:20] Liam: one last ask — security packet and SOC 2 evidence please, our compliance team will need that for the dedicated path.
[21:27] Maya: we'll include SOC2, SAML/SSO notes, and audit-log examples in the doc share.
[21:33] (meeting close) Maya: thanks everyone, will follow up with the bench sheet and configs.

End of transcript.
